hero.lead: A nation of 123 million whose government plans ¥183.8 trillion of bond issuance in fiscal 2026, whose public debt is twice its economy, and whose forests cover two thirds of its land.

capital.heading: The world’s great saver, borrowing from itself.

register.name: JASSO social bonds, fiscal 2026
register.detail: Japan Student Services Organization · 83rd, 84th and 85th series, ¥30bn each, two-year · 85th series priced 21 October 2026, issued 9 November 2026, coupon 1.961%, due 20 November 2028
register.note: Every JASSO bond since the 52nd series is issued as a social bond; FILP agency bonds of ¥120bn are planned for fiscal 2026
register.text: Social bonds of the Japan Student Services Organization, the independent administrative agency that mainly offers scholarship programmes to students. Since the 72nd series its bonds follow its Social Finance Framework, with a second-party opinion from Japan Credit Rating Agency. Its scholarships help students meet the cost of study, which serves the education standard.

register.name: 5-Year Japan Climate Transition Bonds (6)
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · auctioned 2 November 2026 · issued 4 November 2026 · due 20 September 2031 · coupon 2.2% · competitive bids ¥959.9bn
register.note: Issued under the fiscal 2026 JGB issuance plan; five-year and ten-year Climate Transition Bonds were also auctioned on 25 May and 24 August 2026
register.text: The sixth issue of five-year Japan Climate Transition Bonds, sovereign bonds issued under the Japan Climate Transition Bond Framework, revised in June 2025, with a published list of potential allocation projects for fiscal 2026. They finance the Government’s green transformation (GX) investment toward a decarbonised economy, which bears on the energy standard.

register.name: FY2026 JGB Issuance Plan
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · fiscal year from April 2026 · initial plan of 26 December 2025, ¥180.7tn · revised 3 June 2026 for the supplementary budget · calendar-based market issuance ¥168.5tn
register.note: Special deficit-financing bonds raised by ¥3.1tn to ¥26.0tn; refunding bonds unchanged at ¥135.8tn
register.text: Total government bond issuance for fiscal 2026, raised by ¥3,113.5 billion to ¥183,805.5 billion when the Ministry of Finance altered the plan on 3 June 2026 for the supplementary budget; the increase is in special deficit-financing bonds. The initial plan reduced super-long issuance, based on dialogue with the market.

register.name: Fiscal Investment and Loan Program, fiscal 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · FILP plan for fiscal 2026 · up ¥6.8tn on fiscal 2025 · education ¥838.3bn · housing ¥708.4bn · welfare and medical care ¥440.5bn · SMEs and micro enterprises ¥1,933.6bn
register.note: Most of the increase supports the Japan-U.S. Strategic Investment Initiative: overseas investments and loans of ¥10,393.0bn
register.text: The programme of long-term public loans and investment for fiscal 2026 totals ¥19,018.0 billion, an increase of ¥6.8 trillion on fiscal 2025. Within it, education receives ¥838.3 billion, housing ¥708.4 billion, welfare and medical care ¥440.5 billion and small, medium and micro enterprises ¥1,933.6 billion, which serve the education, shelter, health and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Forest across two thirds of the land: timber, water and carbon in a crowded nation.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 11.2% are under fifteen: an ageing nation whose people hold one of the world’s great stores of savings.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: A fifth of the power renewable, with offshore wind and geothermal still to come.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Second Harvest Japan
items.text: Japan’s first food bank, a certified non-profit that collects donated food and passes it to people in need through its own pantries and 472 partner organisations; in 2024 it handled 1,318,744 kg of donated food, equal to 2,491,155 meals, for 1.03 million people, and in July 2026 it was one of the first four food banks certified by the Consumer Affairs Agency.

items.name: Kuradashi
items.text: A company founded in 2014 that buys surplus food and goods from manufacturers before their best-by dates and sells them online at a discount, giving a portion of proceeds to social causes; since January 2025 it also offers a logistics service with over 150 partner warehouses to cut food loss in supply chains.

items.name: WOTA
items.text: A company founded in 2014 that builds small-scale decentralised systems to regenerate and reuse household wastewater; after the 2024 Noto Peninsula earthquake it deployed 100 WOTA BOX units and 207 handwashing stands, supporting 89% of evacuation centres with prolonged water outages and 68 medical and welfare facilities.

items.name: Homedoor
items.text: A certified non-profit in Osaka working to end homelessness, which runs a shelter of 42 rooms in two buildings and HUBchari, a bike-share service at about 700 locations that gives work to people experiencing homelessness; it has supported the lives of more than 7,000 people and given employment support to more than 500.

items.name: Katariba
items.text: A certified non-profit founded in 2001 that provides learning opportunities and support to children who do not attend school, including Room K, an online programme run with participating municipalities and public funding; in October 2025 it agreed a pilot with The Nippon Foundation and four local governments to reduce non-attendance.

items.name: Florence
items.text: One of Japan’s largest certified non-profits in child welfare, whose main revenue is its own business income: its home-visit care for sick children, with 150,000 cases to date and no serious accident, serves 34 cities and 23 wards around Tokyo from April 2026, and it also runs medical day care and a children’s food outreach programme.

items.name: Ory Laboratory (OryLab)
items.text: A company that makes OriHime avatar robots and runs DAWN, a café in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, where people with severe disabilities or intractable diseases who have difficulty going out serve customers by operating the robots remotely; in 2025 it trained people facing mobility challenges in Aarhus, Denmark, as pilots.
